title: Privilege and Procurement Governance Manual
author: Mariana Ortiz
content:
Overview

This manual consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies for: access and permissions (privilege lifecycle), change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor management, and corporate travel. It provides concrete workflows, approval matrices, example templates, and audit controls to ensure consistent decision-making across teams.

Scope

- Applicable to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendor representatives.
- Includes hosted, dedicated, and private deployment engagements where procurement, data, or privileged access is involved.
- Excludes team-level tactical guides; those should link back to the canonical sections below.

Document structure

1) Access & Permissions Lifecycle
2) Change Management Procedures
3) Data Classification & Handling
4) Procurement and Expense Controls
5) Vendor Onboarding and Offboarding
6) Travel Policy: approvals and reimbursements
7) Templates and Forms
8) Roles, Ownership, and Audit Controls
9) Appendix: sample policies and CLI snippets

1) Access & Permissions Lifecycle

Purpose: minimize blast radius by enforcing least privilege and a repeatable lifecycle for granting, reviewing, and revoking access.

Key principles:
- Just-in-time (JIT) access for high-privilege operations.
- Role-based access (RBAC) for services; attribute-based exceptions only when documented.
- Quarterly privileged access reviews for owner teams.

Roles and owners:
- Requestor: employee or service owner who requests access.
- Approver: manager + resource owner (two-person approval for privilege > role:admin).
- IAM Team: enforces RBAC templates and emergency access policies.

Privilege request workflow (standard):
1. Requestor opens the Access Request template in the IT portal (link in staff handbook).
2. Provide: justification, duration, least-permissions required, and related ticket id.
3. Manager approves (business justification).
4. Resource owner approves (technical fit).
5. IAM Team issues access with audit tags and expiry.

High-risk (examples): production DB write, KMS HSM operations, deployment promotion tokens. These require time-bound JIT via the jumpbox or one-time temporary tokens valid ≤ 8 hours.

Quarterly review schedule:
- Owners run the Privileged Access Report (P-Audit) on the first Monday of each quarter.
- Identify: unused privileges > 30 days, service accounts with login rights, and orphaned permissions.
- Remediation SLA: 14 days for revoking or documenting exception with risk acceptance.

Access matrix (summary table):
| Resource class | Typical roles | Approval threshold | Default TTL | Escalation path |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Prod GPU fleet | gpu-operator, gpu-viewer | Owner + Manager | 24h JIT | SRE oncall -> Director Infra |
| Customer data store | db-reader, db-analyst | Legal + Data Owner | 7d | Security -> CISO |
| KMS/HSM | kms-admin | CISO + Security Eng | 4h JIT | Security SOC |

Emergency access (break glass):
- Logged via PagerDuty incident with a ticket created in the incident tracker.
- Access automatically revoked after incident closure and recorded in the post-incident review.

2) Change Management Procedures

Objective: ensure predictable, low-risk changes to services, infra, and data schemas.

Change types:
- Standard (pre-authorized): routine updates with runbook, low-risk (e.g., configuration flip).
- Minor: requires change request, low impact, scheduled maintenance window.
- Major: architecture changes, migrations—requires full change advisory board (CAB) review.
- Emergency: immediate mitigation; after-action review required.

Pre-change checklist (must be completed before scheduling):
- Rollback plan documented and validated.
- Load/latency/runbook SLOs defined.
- Backups verified and stored off-cluster.
- Stakeholder notification list completed.

Change approval matrix (summary):
| Change type | Approver(s) | Lead time | Communication |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Standard | Service owner | 0-2 business days | Slack #service-updates |
| Minor | Service owner + Infra | 3 business days | Email + Jira notice |
| Major | CAB (Product, Infra, Security) | 7+ business days | Company-wide status + runbook |
| Emergency | Exec oncall + CSM (if customer impact) | Immediate | Incident channel + postmortem |

Post-change validation steps:
1. Run automated health checks.
2. Compare key metrics to baseline (latency, errors, token throughput).
3. If metrics deviate > defined threshold (10% latency, 5% error rate), trigger rollback.

3) Data Classification & Handling

Classification labels: Public, Internal, Confidential, Regulated (customer PII/PHI).

Minimum controls by classification:
- Public: no special controls.
- Internal: encryption at rest, company-only access.
- Confidential: encryption at rest and transit, MFA for access, logging.
- Regulated: data residency enforcement, DLP scanning, contractual controls.

Data handling table:
| Data class | Storage requirement | Access control | Retention | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Internal | Encrypted S3 | Group-based RBAC | 2 years | Team lead |
| Confidential | Encrypted S3 + restricted buckets | IAM + approval | 7 years | Data steward |
| Regulated | Customer-dedicated VPC/storage | Legal-approved access only | Per contract | Legal/Data Privacy |

Data transfer and export:
- Export of Regulated data requires Data Use Agreement (DUA) and explicit Legal sign-off.
- Use the redwood-data-transfer CLI to initiate and log cross-region transfers:

$ redwood-data-transfer start --dataset dataset-id --destination eu-west-1 --ticket TKT-1234

4) Procurement and Expense Controls

Principles: transparency, least-cost competitive sourcing, and mapped approvals based on dollar thresholds.

Approval thresholds (examples):
- <= $2,000: Team lead approval.
- $2,001–$25,000: Department head + procurement review.
- $25,001–$250,000: Procurement + Legal + Finance VP.
- > $250,000: Executive committee review (CFO + CEO + Head of Procurement).

Procurement workflow (summary):
1. Create a procurement request in SpendTrack with business justification and estimated TCO.
2. Procurement sources 2–3 quotes (exceptions for single-source with justification).
3. Legal reviews contractual terms for data residency, indemnities, and termination.
4. Finance approves budget and issues PO.
5. Vendor onboarding (see Section 5).

Expense policy highlights:
- Cardholders must reconcile within 7 business days of expense.
- Per-diem and mileage rates are published in the Travel section.
- Non-compliant expenses are flagged and may require repayment.

Sample PO template (fields):
| PO field | Required | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Vendor name | Yes | Registered legal entity |
| Contract term | Yes | Start/end dates |
| Data handling clause | Yes | Attach DPA if applicable |
| Payment terms | Yes | Net-30 default |

5) Vendor Onboarding and Offboarding

Onboarding checklist:
- Security questionnaire completed (SSQ score threshold 80%).
- DPA executed for vendors handling Confidential or Regulated data.
- Network access scoped to minimal CIDR ranges and service ports.
- Audit logging configured and retained per contract.
- Designated vendor liaison and internal owner assigned.

Network and credential rules:
- Vendor service accounts must use short-lived keys and OAuth flows where supported.
- Shared accounts are prohibited unless controlled with a vault and rotation policy.

Offboarding steps (mandatory):
1. Disable all vendor accounts and API keys.
2. Revoke network access (security group/cidr rules).
3. Confirm data deletion or handback terms per contract.
4. Archive contract and close PO in SpendTrack.

6) Travel Policy: approvals and reimbursements

Booking and approvals:
- All company travel booked through the approved Travel Portal; exceptions require manager sign-off.
- International travel for employees handling Regulated data requires a pre-travel security review.

Per diem and allowable expenses:
- Domestic per diem: $75/day.
- International per diem: country-specific (see travel portal).
- Allowed: airfare (economy or premium if >6 hours travel), lodging (standard business), ground transport, meal expenses.
- Disallowed: personal entertainment, lavish upgrades without exec pre-approval.

Reimbursement steps:
1. Submit expense in ExpenseIt within 7 days with receipts attached.
2. Manager approves or returns for clarification within 3 business days.
3. Finance processes payment within the next payroll cycle.

Risk note: employees on travel must not transfer Regulated data to personal devices. Use company laptop with disk encryption and corporate VPN.

7) Templates and Forms (links and samples)

- Access Request Template (use for privilege lifecycle).
- Change Request Form (include risk, rollback, stakeholders).
- Procurement Request (SpendTrack entry template).
- Vendor Security Assessment (SSQ).
- Travel Authorization Form.

Example: Access Request minimal fields:
- requester_name:
- email:
- requested_role:
- resource_id:
- justification:
- duration(hours/days):
- manager_approval:
- resource_owner_approval:

8) Roles, Responsibilities, and Escalation

- People Ops: governance, training, and quarterly audit scheduling.
- IAM Team: implement RBAC templates, JIT tools, and run access reports.
- Procurement: sourcing, PO issuance, vendor contracting.
- Legal: DPA and contract review for privacy and indemnity.
- Security (CISO): approve high-risk vendor access and incident response lead.

Escalation paths:
- Policy exceptions: People Ops -> VP People Ops -> Legal (if data risk) -> CEO approval for >$250k spends.
- Security incidents: Security SOC -> CISO -> Exec oncall.

9) Enforcement, Audit, and Metrics

Key controls to be measured monthly:
- % of privileged accounts with TTL set (target >95%).
- % of procurement requests with 2+ quotes (target 90%).
- Time-to-revoke for offboarded vendor accounts (target <24 hours).
- Completed quarterly privileged access reviews by owner (target 100%).

Audit cadence:
- Internal audit: semi-annual review led by People Ops + Internal Audit.
- External audit: annually for Regulated data vendors (SOC2 / ISO where applicable).

Non-compliance handling:
- First instance: remediation plan and training.
- Repeat violations: disciplinary process per People Ops policy.

Appendix A: sample CLI snippets

- Revoke all keys for vendor-service-id:
$ vault revoke -entity vendor-service-id --reason "offboarded"

- Generate privileged JIT token (example):
$ redwood-iam request-jit --role kms-admin --duration 4h --ticket TKT-456
